entities.summary:
Al-Kamal ibn al-Humam was a prominent Egyptian Hanafi-Maturidi, polymath, legal theorist and jurist, born in unknown and died in 1457. He was a mujtahid and highly regarded in many sciences of knowledge, including fiqh, usul al-fiqh, kalam, logic, Sufism, Arabic language and literature, tafsir, Hadith, Islamic law of inheritance, mathematics, and music. Ibn al-Humam was also a Sufi and a scholar of Hadith, whose works on these subjects were widely studied and respected. His legal theories, particularly in the areas of fiqh and usul al-fiqh, had a significant impact on the development of Islamic law in the Middle East and North Africa. Ibn al-Humam's contributions to the fields of Islamic jurisprudence and Sufism continue to be studied and debated by scholars today.

In addition to his legal and Sufi works, Ibn al-Humam was also a scholar of Arabic language and literature, whose translations of classical texts into Arabic were widely acclaimed. His love of music and mathematics also earned him recognition as a polymath, with his works on these subjects still studied by scholars today.

Despite his many contributions to various fields, Ibn al-Humam's personal life remains somewhat of a mystery, with little information available about his family or education. However, his influence on Islamic thought and law is undeniable, and his works continue to be studied and respected by scholars around the world.

Ibn al-Humam's legacy is also evident in the many institutions and schools that bear his name, including the Ibn al-Humam University in Cairo, which was founded in the 19th century to promote Islamic studies and legal scholarship.

In conclusion, Al-Kamal ibn al-Humam was a highly respected scholar and jurist, whose contributions to Islamic law, Sufism, and Arabic language and literature continue to be felt today.
